questions: How is each entry of Pascal's triangle built from the row above?
Which row gives the coefficients of (a + b)^4?
segments.say: Start with the triangle. Each row lists the coefficients of a binomial expansion: row n belongs to (a + b)^n, the edges are 1, and every other entry is the sum of the two entries above it. Build row 4 together: 1, 4, 6, 4, 1 - keep it on the board, we will spend it in a few minutes.

questions: In term r + 1, what happens to the powers of a and b as r rises?
What is C(3, 1) and where does it sit in the triangle?
segments.say: Now the theorem that uses the triangle: (a + b)^n is the sum of C(n, r) a^(n - r) b^r. Watch the pointer build (a + b)^3 term by term - coefficients 1, 3, 3, 1, powers of a falling 3, 2, 1, 0 while the powers of b climb to meet them.

questions: Why must the -3 stay in brackets in (2x - 3)^4?
Which terms of the expansion are negative, and why?
segments.say: Spend row 4 on a harder case: expanding (2x - 3)^4. Each term is C(4, r) (2x)^(4 - r) (-3)^r. Stress the brackets around -3: its odd powers are negative and its even powers positive, so the signs alternate, ending at 16x^4 - 96x^3 + 216x^2 - 216x + 81.

questions: Where is the missing 2ab in the area picture?
segments.say: Here is the trap, sprung on purpose: it is tempting to square each part of a sum separately. But the numbers refuse - (1 + 2)^2 is 9 while 1^2 + 2^2 is only 5 - and the area picture shows the two missing a-by-b rectangles that make up 2ab.

questions: What is the general term of (a + b)^n?
Why do the signs alternate in (2x - 3)^4?
segments.say: Now work through the worksheet in pairs, checking each expansion against the trap section of your student notes. Last, the exit ticket - on your own, no talking - and remember: coefficients from the triangle, powers of a falling, powers of b rising, negatives in brackets.
segments.watchFor: (a + b)^2 = a^2 + b^2. Listen for students who drop the middle term when they square a sum. Send them back to the numbers: The missing middle term 2ab is the whole trap: (1 + 2)^2 is 9, not 5.
